notes: On 29 January 2024, IDF tanks opened fire on a civilian vehicle in an hours-long attack and killed 7 people inside (2 adults and 5 minors) near the Faris Gas Station in Gaza - Tal el Hawa (Gaza City, Gaza Strip). The tanks opened fire at the vehicle (via machine guns mounted on it) early in the morning, initially killing 2 adult parents and 3 children (2 girls and one boy). The 2 injured survivors of the initial attack (a 15-year-old child from the same family and her 5-year-old cousin Hind Rajab) called the Palestinian Red Crescent Society (PRCS) for help, reporting their situation and remaining in the vehicle for hours waiting to be rescued until they were also killed by the consecutive tank fires in the afternoon and in the evening. The presence of the Israeli forces in the area prevented access to reach and retrieve the victims' bodies until 12 days after the incident. Even though the IDF initially denied responsibility amid the global outrage over the incident, various independent investigations concluded that there were Israeli tanks present at the scene but no Hamas operatives/active clashes around, and tank crews should have been able to determine that the persons in the vehicle did not pose a threat.
